clue.text: One in do with "lazing" rule, perhaps?

definitions.text: One in do with "lazing" rule, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the three words could be arranged some other way, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone at a party seems to live by the motto of idling about.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DO, LAZING and RULE rearrange into the twelve letters of the answer; read whole, the clue describes such a person: someone at a party (a do) whose rule is lazing.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth idler who hangs around bars and parties, chasing company, is the classic party-going loafer described.

clue.text: Turn up in defeat mostly as a form of reasoning

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
mostly says the word for defeat loses its final letter

parts.note: to lick an opponent is to defeat them

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for turn is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: A thinker ponders how failure can be explained rationally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LICK to LIC; 'up' turns GO into OG, which goes 'in' to make L-OG-IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Systematic deductive thinking is a discipline of sound argument and inference.

clue.text: Regular style of dress

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means unvarying, consistent
the standard outfit worn by members of a group such as a school or army

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of sameness: constant in form, and identical clothing worn by all.

clue.text: Work unit arises to get involved with the fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, arises says the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
to engage with something is to get involved with it

explanation.surface: A labourer rises to take part in the fruit harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arises' turns ERG into GRE, followed by ENGAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenish variety of plum is a stone fruit.

clue.text: See 1
One obsessed person grabbing page as data for computer

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: grabbing says the word for an obsessed person holds another piece

parts.note: a fanatic, as in health nut, is a nut

explanation.surface: A fanatic snatches a sheet of paper full of figures to feed the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Information fed into a computer for processing is what users key in.

clue.text: Store records in Bow -a place that's buzzing

parts.note: a bow is a curve or arc
a beehive buzzes with bees

explanation.surface: Records are kept in Bow, a busy part of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is also a district of East London, which makes it look like a place name rather than ARC.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to keep documents in a repository for preservation is to file them away permanently.

clue.text: Timer damaged with dent Cause of damage?

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of the two words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A clock has been knocked about and dented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals an anagram of TIMER with DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmful or injurious is a source of harm, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One tinged with slackness is fired

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: with slackness suggests the word tinged is loosened and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A slightly coloured lazy person gets the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with slackness' signals the anagram, placed after I. 'fired' looks like dismissed from a job, but here means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Set alight, kindled, as a fire or fuse is when lit.

clue.text: Work at a business centre in obscurity

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Someone toils at a firm in a commercial hub, unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the square mile of London that houses its banks and finance houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of transparency or clarity, so murkiness or unclearness.

clue.text: Girl in government department with a new pet?

indicators.note: in says the girl's name goes inside the department

parts.note: DTI was the UK Department of Trade and Industry
Alma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman working in a ministry brings along a fresh animal.
explanation.walkthrough: DTI is the former British Department of Trade and Industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted breed of dog, the question mark showing it is one example of a household animal.

clue.text: Tell in a certain jargon one to work on the balance

definitions.text: one to work on the balance

parts.note: a certain indicates an indefinite one, the article a

indicators.note: in says the word for tell goes inside the word for jargon

parts.note: cant is the special jargon of a group
to tell is to count, as with votes or beads

explanation.surface: Explain something using a particular specialist language to someone balancing the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookkeeping professional prepares the balance sheet and works on the financial balance.

clue.text: River goddess

definitions.meaning: the Thames is so called as it flows through Oxford
the Egyptian goddess, wife of Osiris

explanation.definitionFit: The name serves both for the Oxford stretch of the Thames and for an Egyptian deity.

clue.text: Butterfly's particular mark

definitions.meaning: a butterfly with ragged wings and a white mark on its underside
a punctuation mark marking a short pause

explanation.definitionFit: The butterfly is named after the white comma-shaped mark on its wings; the other sense is punctuation.

clue.text: Applauded at college and became less depressed

parts.note: applauded means cheered
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: A student received an ovation on campus and felt better.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grew happier, lifted in spirits after feeling low.

clue.text: Scot with boat going round river for a fish

parts.note: Mac, the Gaelic patronymic, is a nickname for a Scotsman

indicators.note: going round says the boat word surrounds another letter

parts.note: keel is used for a flat-bottomed boat, or by metonymy for a ship

explanation.surface: A Scotsman sails his vessel round the estuary hoping to catch dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An oily striped sea fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: The repartee when angry at informal address

parts.note: cross means angry
a talk is an informal speech or address

explanation.surface: Banter turns sharp when someone is irritated by a casual speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Witty exchange of remarks, quick-fire banter between people.

clue.text: Dull cricketer around end of game whacked out

parts.note: dead can mean dull, lifeless

indicators.note: around says the cricketer word goes about another letter

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of game

explanation.surface: A boring batsman is utterly exhausted after the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted, worn out, the slang sense of being tired.

clue.text: Force the fiery being to take in oxygen

indicators.note: to take in says the creature holds the letter for oxygen

parts.note: a dragon breathes fire
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A fire-breathing beast inhales air.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce or press someone into doing something, as soldiers once were press-ganged.

clue.text: Cycle that I broke partly in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone admits to partly smashing a bicycle while withdrawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' finds TIBRO in 'that I broke'; 'in retreat' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A path round a planet or star is one revolution, a circuit or round trip.

clue.text: Help one in difficulties (in trouble in a fight)

indicators.note: in places the word for trouble inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match
to ail is to trouble, afflict

explanation.surface: Rescue a person struggling, who has got hurt in a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone financially or from a predicament is a rescue package.

clue.text: A region in the Far East

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the words that follow, running across both

explanation.surface: A zone in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'A' as definition and 'region in' as indicator; 'region' must be part of the definition, and 'in' alone signals the letters inside 'Far East'.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or zone, a tract of territory.

clue.text: Side possibly short in willingness for group work

parts.note: a side, as in sport, is an example of a team
in British pubs a short is a small measure of spirits such as whisky

explanation.surface: A team is down a player but still keen.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'short' is British slang for a shot of spirits; 'short' seems to describe the side being under strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooperative enthusiasm and loyalty among members of a squad.

clue.text: Groups of bones that could be seen in Gibraltar (sight seeing)

indicators.note: could be seen in says the answer is visible inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Bones may be spotted on a tour of the Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle-bone sets of the foot, plural of the anatomical term for the ankle area.

clue.text: The inhabitants of an island flower with a bit of hooley

parts.note: the iris is a flower

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the first letter of hooley

explanation.surface: Islanders at a lively party, one with a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooley is an Irish word for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Ireland, an island nation.

clue.text: Close meeting and switch to accommodate day in the continent

indicators.note: to accommodate says the shuffled letters hold another piece
switch says the letters of the little word are changed round

parts.note: jour is the French word for day, as said on the Continent

explanation.surface: End a session and move on to fit in a day in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' rearranges AND into ADN, which 'to accommodate' wraps round the French for day; 'Close meeting' looks like a description of a near encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a session to an end or suspend it until later.

clue.text: City's description of traffic bollard using few words

parts.note: LA is the abbreviation for Los Angeles, a city
a traffic cone is cone-shaped, so conic describes it

explanation.surface: A city describes its road markers briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse and concise, brief in speech like the Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: A drawing with B?

parts.note: B is a grade of the writing tool used by artists, so a picture made with one

explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing made with a graphite stick, of which B marks a soft grade.

clue.text: See 25
